To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the IFT cycle is divided into four phases, (2) IFT particles are functionally and structurally remodeled during the cycle, and (3) the IFT machinery is composed of multiple complexes that can interact genetically.
the analysis of flagellar mutants and the genetic interactions among these mutants provide a powerful tool to study the structure and function, as well as the biogenesis, of cilia and IFT particles.
conditional flagellar mutants provide a useful tool for the analysis of intraflagellar transport at the molecular level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the genetic and molecular basis of flagellar assembly in Chlamy domonas.
understanding the molecular basis of cilia formation and the role of cilia in human health and disease.
the analysis of the molecular mechanisms of flagellar assembly, the identification of proteins involved in this process, and the characterization of their function by genetic and phenotypic analyses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Chlamydomonassystem is a powerful tool to analyze ciliary function, structure, and biogenesis.
Chlamydomonad flagellar mutants have been and continue to be a powerful tool to understand the molecular mechanisms underlying cilia assembly.
conditional fla mutants provide a unique tool to analyze IFT at the molecular level and to identify and characterize the components and functions of IFT particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IFT is a dynamic process that involves the remodeling of IFT particle structure and function at both flagellar ends.
Chlamydomonaspresents a powerful genetic system to study the structure and function IFT particles, their motors, and their role in flagellar assembly and maintenance.

the analysis of conditional fla mutants has revealed a number of interesting interactions among genes encoding proteins that are part of the same IFT particle and/or that function in the same step of flagellar assembly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IFT particles are highly dynamic, with a complex structure and function, and that the IFT system is a highly interconnected and integrated network.

IFT particles are not simply a collection of cargo proteins but that the composition of IFT particles changes in a highly coordinated fashion as the particles move from one end of the cilium to the other.
the IFT system is highly conserved in evolution and that it is possible to identify IFT genes in any organism that has flagella.
